events.continuity_hook: Moves the Boston family trip from narrowed options into booking while the preferred nonstop flights and Back Bay hotel are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Boston flights and hotel, select the family seating plan, and capture the practical arrival and breakfast notes.
events.scenario_brief: Maya and her spouse are ready to book the four-night July Boston family weekend after deciding that the Back Bay hotel with larger rooms and easy nearby meals is the best fit. The waterfront option still has stronger reviews but costs noticeably more, and the Cambridge option includes breakfast but would make the first two sightseeing mornings less convenient. The late-morning nonstop outbound and early-afternoon nonstop return are still available for three travelers. Remaining items are confirming the hotel rate is cancellable, choosing seats that keep their child with at least one parent, deciding whether to add checked bags now, and noting easy breakfast options near the hotel since breakfast is not included.

events.continuity_hook: Final logistics pass for the Boston family weekend after bookings are complete and minor schedule details have shifted.
events.interaction_goal: Turn the Boston plan into a concise departure checklist and decide whether any seat or transfer changes are worth making.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Boston trip, the nonstop flights and Back Bay hotel are booked. The airline has nudged the return departure slightly later, which still keeps the family home at a reasonable hour, and the hotel confirms luggage storage if the room is not ready on arrival. Their seats are together on the outbound, but the return has one parent across the aisle from the other two. The forecast points to hot afternoons with a chance of storms, and the first evening dinner plan is still loose. Remaining items are ATL arrival timing, Logan-to-hotel transfer choice, whether to keep checking for a better return seat grouping, and how much to plan for breakfast outside the hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new work-travel episode once the summer family trip is finished and an August client visit appears.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Cleveland trip, identify the practical flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details needed before Maya requests approval.
events.scenario_brief: After the Boston trip, Maya gets a new August client request for three onsite build sessions in Cleveland. The working plan is a Monday arrival, Tuesday and Wednesday full client days, and a Thursday return after a short closeout meeting. Atlanta has several nonstop options to Cleveland, while one-stop fares are only modestly cheaper and add connection risk. The client has not yet confirmed whether sessions will be at the main hospital campus near University Circle or a downtown administrative office. Remaining items are the exact worksite, first required arrival time Tuesday, Thursday finish time, and whether a hotel near the campus or downtown would make the mornings easier.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Cleveland planning after the worksite and client schedule are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main Cleveland flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the approval-ready plan with the tradeoffs clearly summarized.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the Cleveland sessions will be at the hospital campus near University Circle, with a Tuesday 9:00 a.m. start, a full Wednesday onsite day, and a Thursday closeout expected to end by 2:00 p.m. The cleanest outbound is a Monday late-morning nonstop that allows a calm hotel check-in and prep block. For Thursday, a midafternoon nonstop is possible but leaves little margin if the closeout runs long, while an early-evening nonstop gives more breathing room. Hotel choices include a campus-adjacent property with strong guest ratings and on-site dining but paid breakfast, a downtown hotel with included breakfast but rideshare-dependent mornings, and a cheaper airport-area option that would complicate both onsite days.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Cleveland work trip from approval into booking while the selected fare and hotel rate are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Cleveland flights, hotel, seat choices, room request, local transportation notes, and receipt capture.
events.scenario_brief: Maya’s manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop, the Thursday early-evening return, and the campus-adjacent hotel as long as the room remains cancellable. The client confirms rideshares are normal between the airport, hotel, and campus, so no rental car is needed. Breakfast is not included, but the hotel has an early cafe and several dinner choices nearby. Seat maps show window seats available toward the rear on both flights, while forward seats are mostly aisle or middle. Remaining items are completing the booking before the fare changes, adding a quiet-room request, selecting seats, and saving confirmations for reimbursement.

events.continuity_hook: Handles a late client schedule change for the Cleveland work trip after booking but before travel.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move Maya to the later return flight and update the final Cleveland departure checklist accordingly.
events.scenario_brief: About a week before the Cleveland trip, the flights and campus-adjacent hotel are booked, but the client moves Thursday’s closeout from early afternoon to 4:00 p.m. The current early-evening return is now tight if the meeting runs over or traffic is slow, and there is a later nonstop that would make the airport timing calmer. The hotel confirms luggage storage after checkout, and the selected rear window seats are still in place. Remaining items are whether to change the return flight, how late Maya should leave the campus for the airport, whether to keep the same seat if the return changes, and updating the trip file if the fare difference is approved.
